Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can plot the relationship between two patterns, such as those given in the table below, in a coordinate plane.

Content:
| Pattern A: add [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 4] |
| Pattern B: add [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 10] | [MATH: 15] | [MATH: 20] |

Content:
To do this, we choose the horizontal axis ([MATH: x]-axis) to correspond to pattern A and the vertical axis ([MATH: y]-axis) to correspond to pattern B.

Content:
We add one more row to the table that contains the ordered pairs corresponding to each point. Here, the [MATH: x] and [MATH: y]-coordinates are the terms from patterns A and B, respectively.

Content:
| Pattern A: add [MATH: 1] | [MATH: \color{blue}0] | [MATH: \color{blue}1] | [MATH: \color{blue}2] | [MATH: \color{blue}3] | [MATH: \color{blue}4] |
| Pattern B: add [MATH: 5] | [MATH: \color{red}0] | [MATH: \color{red}5] | [MATH: \color{red}10] | [MATH: \color{red}15] | [MATH: \color{red}20] |
| Ordered pair | [MATH: ({\color{blue}0},{\color{red}0})] | [MATH: ({\color{blue}1},{\color{red}5})] | [MATH: ({\color{blue}2},{\color{red}10})] | [MATH: ({\color{blue}3},{\color{red}15})] | [MATH: ({\color{blue}4},{\color{red}20})] |

Item 2 — Example: Plotting a Graph Given a Table Containing Two Patterns

Example Prompt:
Find the numbers for the patterns shown in the table below and plot the corresponding graph.

| Pattern A: add [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 1] | | | |
| Pattern B: multiply by [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 1] | | | |

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The rule of pattern A is "add [MATH: 2]", and the first number is [MATH: 1.] So, we have the following pattern:

[IMG: /graphics/44acea1003d154f12e611e21a4fb0329]

The rule of pattern B is "multiply by [MATH: 2]", and the first number is [MATH: 1.] So, we have the following pattern:

[IMG: /graphics/39f3caa97aae59f0fc1a5755b8ce7deb]

Let's fill in the table:

| Pattern A: add [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 7] |
| Pattern B: multiply by [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 8] |

We choose the horizontal axis ([MATH: x]-axis) to correspond to pattern A and the vertical axis ([MATH: y]-axis) to correspond to pattern B. We add one more row to the table with ordered pairs corresponding to each point.

| Pattern A: add [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 5] | [MATH: 7] |
| Pattern B: multiply by [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 8] |
| Ordered pair | [MATH: (1,1)] | [MATH: (3,2)] | [MATH: (5,4)] | [MATH: (7,8)] |

Plotting each ordered pair on the coordinate plane, we get the following graph:

[IMG: /graphics/e3c5daa55f2e1d46e561d0ded4e13f1e]
